Confidence intervals for the parameters of a fitted pglmm

Source: R/pglmm-confint.R
confint.communityPGLMM.Rd

Confidence intervals for the fixed effects and the variances of the random terms of a model fitted by pglmm() or pglmm_compare().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'communityPGLMM'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

A model fitted by pglmm() or pglmm_compare().

parm

The parameters: names (the names of the fixed effects, and of the random terms as in VarCorr(), e.g. "1|sp__", and "residual") or positions in the rows of the result; "fixed" for all the fixed effects, "random" for all the variances. Default: all.

level

The confidence level.

...

Ignored.

Value

A matrix with one row for each parameter (fixed effects, then the variances of the random terms) and two columns, the lower and upper limits.

Details

For the fixed effects, the intervals are Wald intervals, from the estimates and their standard errors (B and B.se of the fitted model).

For the variances of the random terms (and the residual variance of gaussian models), the intervals are profile likelihood intervals: the values of a variance where the (restricted, for REML = TRUE) log-likelihood maximized over the other parameters is qchisq(level, 1) / 2 below its maximum, as confint(method = "profile") of lme4 and glmmTMB. They are not symmetric, and include zero when the data are consistent with no variance for a term (Wald intervals of variances are not reliable there). They show how well the data separate the variances of paired terms, such as a phylogenetic term (1 | sp__) and its non-phylogenetic partner (1 | sp): when the two are hard to separate, both intervals are wide. Each limit needs several fits of the model with the variance fixed, so for large models, use parm to choose the variances of interest. They are available for models fitted with bayes = FALSE and either sparse = TRUE (gaussian models; the default when the model has phylogenies) or method = "Laplace" (the default for binomial and poisson models). Penalized quasi-likelihood (method = "PQL") has no likelihood to profile, and models fitted with sparse = FALSE keep no sparse factorization; their variances get NA. The variances of terms with a covariance matrix (e.g. a phylogeny) are on the scale of the standardized matrix, as s2r and s2n of the fitted model: multiply them by scale_factors to compare them with other terms (see VarCorr()).

For models fitted with bayes = TRUE, the intervals are the 95% credible intervals reported by INLA (B.ci, s2r.ci, s2n.ci and s2resid.ci).

See also

VarCorr(), pglmm_profile_LRT().

Examples

# community data: abundance of each species at each site
dat <- data.frame(
  site = rep(rownames(comm_a), times = ncol(comm_a)),
  sp = rep(colnames(comm_a), each = nrow(comm_a)),
  freq = unlist(comm_a, use.names = FALSE)
)
dat$shade <- envi$shade[match(dat$site, envi$site)]
phy <- ape::keep.tip(phylotree, unique(dat$sp))
fit <- pglmm(freq ~ shade + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site),
  data = dat, cov_ranef = list(sp = phy)
)
confint(fit)
#>                    2.5 %     97.5 %
#> (Intercept) -1.384258059 0.83991193
#> shade        0.009499427 0.03588418
#> 1|sp         0.000000000 1.91066115
#> 1|sp__       0.000000000 2.14640273
#> 1|site       0.000000000 0.25996778
#> residual     2.710426523 3.97896486
